question.worked_solution:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}={x}^{-2} & \,⟹\,v=\int {x}^{-2}\,dx=-{x}^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{-2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv{|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(-{x}^{-1}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}}-{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}(-{x}^{-1})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =[-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{{e}^{2}}-(-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{1})]+{\int }_{1}^{{e}^{2}}{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})}{{e}^{2}}+(-{x}^{-1}){|}_{1}^{{e}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{2}{{e}^{2}}+(-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}+1) \\  & =1-\frac{3}{{e}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{3}{{e}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
